key_insight: Virtual distillation can be extended from qubit systems to bosonic quantum hardware using multi-copy linear-optical measurements to suppress noise in observable estimates.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical error-mitigation path for bosonic and continuous-variable quantum processors by enabling cleaner measurements of number operators, phase shifts, and quadratures with experimentally available optics.
method: Diagonalize cyclic shift operators with passive linear-optical interferometers.
Use multi-copy measurements to estimate virtually distilled expectation values.
Recover higher-order number correlators via the photon-number characteristic function.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports applying the framework to photon-loss and dephasing noise models and quantifying the suppression of their contributions in virtually distilled observables.
watch_item: The approach relies on access to multiple copies of the same noisy bosonic state and precise interferometric implementations, which may increase experimental overhead and sensitivity to setup imperfections.
paper_title: Error Mitigation in Bosonic Systems via Virtual Distillation
